# AUDIO PROFILE
The old lady: an Englishwoman of the old school in her eighties who has run the bunker's kitchen for five years and is frightened of nothing.

## THE SCENE
A vast, silent, spotless white room. The hundred survivors in white suits stand close around a giant rainbow-sheened silicon wafer the size of a house, the time machine, and understand for the first time what it will cost them. Utter hush, no echo; voices close, quiet and full of feeling.

### DIRECTOR'S NOTES
Emotion for this line: quiet and grave, steady, asking for all of them; two words, the question falls rather than rises.
Style: no softness and no comfort; a stern, grave old woman who has seen the worst happen and is choosing, with total conviction, to risk everything to undo it; low, firm and deliberate, every word meant, steel under the age in her voice; no tears, no smile.
Pace: two quiet words, unhurried, the question falling at the end; no long pauses.
Accent: old-fashioned Received Pronunciation, as heard on the BBC in the 1950s; clipped, precise, Home Counties. Never American.

### SAMPLE CONTEXT
The voice you'd cast as the formidable grandmother in a British drama who everyone, including the robot, does what she says.
